view.stem: 某地区已经能够发电，但电能尚未送到工厂、交通运输设施和居民生活的用电地点。按照电气化中电能获得、传输和应用之间的关系，要补全从发电到实际用电的过程，后续设施应承担怎样的作用？

options.text: 输电设施把电能送到用电地点，用电设备把电能转换为所需的其他形式。
用电设备把电能送到用电地点，输电设施把电能转换为所需的其他形式。
输电设施把电能送到用电地点，用电设备把所需的其他形式能量转换为电能。
用电设备把电能送到用电地点，输电设施把所需的其他形式能量转换为电能。

intent.task: Determine the missing transmission and application functions in one complete generation-to-use process, rather than equate existing generating capacity with widespread actual electrical-energy use.
intent.source_solution: Reuse the independent solution frozen before alternatives in independent-solutions-b92.md, SHA-256 5cae5b7bac81ca31650e05fefb04c0a683466a09c10ce2585d6639094e6b8e0c; no source solution was rerun. Electrification is widespread use of electrical energy in production, transport, and daily life. Generating facilities provide electrical energy, transmission facilities deliver it to the use sites, and use equipment converts it into the other forms required there. In the Soviet historical example, constructing generating facilities expands available electrical energy but does not replace delivery and application. The scenario has already supplied the generating stage, so the missing functions are delivery of electrical energy and its conversion at the use site. No historical name, quantity, political equation, or current data is required.
intent.unit_reason: The two missing functions form one interdependent process-completion judgment. One native single question preserves their facility-to-function mapping and energy-conversion direction; splitting each stage into its own click would fragment the essential relationship. The visible situation applies the definition to an incomplete process rather than asks for a copied definition.
limitations: Recognition of a complete account does not demonstrate independently writing an explanation of electrification.
The generic scenario omits independently explaining the Soviet historical example and its historical contextualization. That part of written seed 1 is not claimed covered.
The application task names production, transport, and daily life but does not assess independently generating examples for each domain.

rationales.derivation: Start from the supplied generating stage. Apply block 1 to assign delivery to transmission facilities and conversion of delivered electrical energy into the required other forms to use equipment. Both missing functions and the conversion direction agree with the definition.

Swap the facility names assigned to the two required functions while retaining the otherwise correct delivery and electrical-to-other-forms wording. The result assigns delivery to use equipment and end-use conversion to transmission facilities, so it does not complete the process defined in block 1.
rationales.misconception: Associate any electrical equipment with moving electricity and treat transmission as its application, reversing the transmission/use facility-to-function mapping.

rationales.derivation: Keep the correct transmission assignment, then reverse the input and output of the application stage: instead of electrical energy becoming the required other forms, make those forms become electrical energy. This replaces end use with a generating-direction conversion.
rationales.misconception: Carry the other-forms-to-electrical direction of generation forward into the use equipment instead of distinguishing generation from application.

rationales.derivation: First exchange the delivery and use facility assignments as in B, then reverse the application-stage conversion direction as in C. The resulting two-clause account has neither the correct delivery role nor the required electrical-to-other-forms use stage.
rationales.misconception: Combine a swapped transmission/use mapping with treating every energy-conversion stage as producing electricity.

view.stem: 三座发电站的发电方式如下：甲利用燃料释放的热产生蒸汽，蒸汽推动汽轮机；乙由流动水直接推动水轮机；丙利用核能产生热，再用蒸汽推动汽轮机。三者都由转动的机器带动发电机。按照主要能源来源分类，下列说法哪些正确？

options.text: 甲属于热电站，开始利用的是燃料的化学能。
乙属于水电站，开始利用的是水的化学能。
丙属于原子能电站，开始利用的是核能。
甲属于水电站，开始利用的是蒸汽的机械能。
乙属于水电站，开始利用的是水流的机械能。
丙属于热电站，开始利用的是燃料的化学能。

intent.task: Classify the three described generating mechanisms by their primary energy source, preserving the distinction between originating energy and shared downstream turbine/generator machinery.
intent.source_solution: Reuse the independently frozen mechanism distinctions without a new source or option solve. Written seed 4 asks for known large generating stations, but this bound seed includes no station names or planned-station account. Specific historical station identities and their type attributions therefore cannot be established from this input and are not claimed covered. The open station-naming and research task remains deferred. For the supplemental mechanism cases, the definition-based solution is fuel chemical energy -> heat -> mechanical energy -> electrical energy for the fuel-thermal mechanism; moving-water mechanical energy -> electrical energy via water turbine and generator for hydroelectric generation; nuclear energy -> heat -> mechanical energy -> electrical energy for the lesson usual nuclear mechanism. Thus the new cases have primary sources chemical, moving-water mechanical, and nuclear respectively. A common generator or steam-turbine stage does not make the primary sources equal.
intent.unit_reason: All three descriptions are one coherent classification task under one primary-energy criterion. Native multiple selection evaluates the definite type-and-source assertions directly rather than creates separate yes/no questions, one question per printed entry, or a combination-code answer. Fuel-thermal versus nuclear classification remains substantive despite their common steam/turbine stage, and the water case tests mechanical energy rather than treating water as a fuel.
limitations: Selecting classification assertions does not demonstrate independently naming, describing, or researching large historical stations.

The source-grounded generic mechanism cases omit the named historical examples requested as one possible response in written seed 4; recall of those names and their historical association is deferred.
No largest-station ranking, current operating fact, or unsupported named thermal station is assessed or inferred.
The selected nuclear definition is copied in full in the seed, but siting/economic reasoning and historical contextualization are not assessed by this classification item.

rationales.derivation: Case 甲 starts with fuel releasing heat. Block 6 identifies this as fuel-thermal generation and places fuel chemical energy before heat, mechanical energy, and electrical energy. Both the type and originating energy match.

Identify the flowing-water case as hydroelectric, then replace its mechanical originating energy with chemical energy by applying the fuel-energy label from block 6 to water. Block 8 explicitly uses moving-water mechanical energy and not burning water as fuel, so the combined assertion is false even though its station label is right.
rationales.misconception: Treat every primary resource as a chemical fuel, carrying the chemical-energy label from a fuel-thermal station over to flowing water.

rationales.derivation: Case 丙 explicitly starts with nuclear energy producing heat. Block 12 defines this nuclear generating mechanism. The subsequent steam/turbine stage does not change its originating nuclear energy or station category.

Begin the description of 甲 at the later steam-pushing-turbine stage and identify moving steam with the moving-water turbine mechanism. This discards the preceding fuel-to-heat step and classifies by an intermediate mechanical transfer rather than the primary chemical source. The full stated mechanism is fuel-thermal, not hydroelectric.
rationales.misconception: Skip the originating energy step and classify a plant as hydroelectric whenever moving water or steam pushes a turbine.

rationales.derivation: Case 乙 has flowing water directly drive a water turbine. Block 8 identifies this as hydroelectric generation using the mechanical energy of flowing water before the generator converts that energy into electrical energy.

Match the steam/turbine stages in 丙 and 甲, then copy both the fuel-thermal label and chemical-energy origin of 甲 onto 丙. This ignores the explicitly stated nuclear heat source. Block 12 preserves the nuclear classification even though downstream steam machinery is shared.
rationales.misconception: Assume every steam-turbine station begins with burning fuel because its downstream machinery resembles a fuel-thermal station.
